name: US inflation
summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September; October data due 10 Nov
state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7%, inside the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). Brent fell to about $98 on 6 Nov, down 7% in a month (Yahoo Finance), which eases one source of upward pressure on the October figure due on 10 Nov.
for_you: Higher prices for fuel, food and services erode household budgets; borrowers with variable-rate debt are most exposed if inflation keeps rates high.
why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
